open_points.subject: R0-97 second-release refused-sign-in counters
open_points.text: During the lockout every sign-in is refused — the right credential included — and is not counted; the lockout is not extended.
open_points.question: In the second release, does “is not counted” exclude a lockout-time sign-in only from A13's throttling window, or also from R0-97's refused-attempt security counter?
options: Exclude it from both counters.
Exclude it only from the throttling window and increment the refused-attempt security counter.
open_points.default_guess: Exclude it only from the throttling window and count it as a refused attempt for the owner.

witness.initial: The second release is running; the fifth wrong credential has started a lockout.
events: A caller attempts a sixth sign-in during the lockout.
The owner later signs in successfully and sees the refused-attempt display.
outcomes: The display reports five refused sign-ins and one lockout.
The display reports six refused sign-ins and one lockout.

open_points.subject: R0-97 refusal-category precedence
open_points.text: shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of the start and of the latest of each kind: refused sign-ins and lockouts; calls on the service API with a token Registry does not know; calls whose token does not allow the operation or class asked; and, apart from these, Kernel's agent-authority calls refused for a session or a project outside its set
open_points.question: When one request satisfies more than one description, which single counter is incremented, or may one request increment several counters; and are “session” and “project outside its set” one kind or two?
options: Use A04's first-failure precedence and increment exactly one counter; combine all Kernel session/set refusals into one kind.
Use A04's first-failure precedence but keep separate Kernel-session and outside-project kinds.
Increment every applicable kind for one request.
open_points.default_guess: Increment exactly one counter according to A04's first-failure precedence, with one combined Kernel authority-refusal kind.
consequences: A single-counter rule makes totals comparable to refused requests and prevents double counting.
Separate Kernel kinds give the owner more diagnostic detail.
Multi-counting can make totals exceed the number of refused requests.
open_points.requirement:
In the second release (R0-100), Registry counts refused attempts in memory from its start and
shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of
the start and of the latest of each kind

open_points.subject: R0-97 counter lifecycle and display
open_points.text:
Registry counts refused attempts in memory from its start and
shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in
open_points.question: Does a successful sign-in or displaying the page clear any security counter, and is the display shown once per owner session or on every qualifying page load?
options: Counters persist until restart and are displayed once immediately after every successful sign-in.
Counters persist until restart and remain visible throughout the owner session.
A successful sign-in or the first display acknowledges and clears them.
open_points.default_guess: Persist until restart and display once immediately after every successful sign-in.
consequences: Persistence preserves evidence across sign-ins but repeatedly shows old attempts.
Clearing on acknowledgement prevents repeated warnings but loses the only in-process history before restart.
Continuous visibility changes more owner-interface results than the stated first page.
open_points.requirement:
The counters hold no value, no credential, no address and no request; a
restart clears them, as it clears the lockout.

open_points.subject: R0-97 recorded counter instants
open_points.text:
with the instant of
the start and of the latest of each kind
open_points.question: What clock supplies these instants, what UTC representation and precision are stored, and how many clock readings does one refused request take when it updates a counter?
options: Use one UTC wall-clock reading per refused request and the process-start UTC reading, represented like other recorded instants.
Derive display instants from monotonic readings plus a wall-clock anchor.
Take separate readings for classification and for each counter updated.
open_points.default_guess: Use one UTC wall-clock reading at process start and one per refused request, represented as the existing UTC-with-time-zone instant at microsecond precision.
consequences: One wall-clock reading gives all counters updated by one request the same instant.
A monotonic-derived timestamp needs an explicit conversion rule and behavior after wall-clock changes.
Several readings can give one refusal different reported instants.
open_points.requirement:
In the second release (R0-100), Registry counts refused attempts in memory from its start and
shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of
the start and of the latest of each kind

open_points.subject: R0-94 retention review selection
open_points.text:
the
customers whose relationship ended, and the archived projects archived, longer
ago than periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: Which configured period applies to each record, in what unit and representation is it supplied, from which date or instant is age computed, and is a record exactly at the threshold shown?
options: Separate customer and project duration settings, compared as exact elapsed durations; show only records strictly older than the threshold.
Calendar-date periods compared in UTC; show records whose due date is today or earlier.
A policy table maps each data kind to a period and comparison rule.
open_points.default_guess: Use separately named customer and project duration settings and show a record only when its UTC age is strictly greater than the configured duration.
consequences: Elapsed durations and calendar periods can produce different due dates around leap years and daylight-saving changes.
Including equality shows a record earlier than the phrase “longer ago than”; excluding it delays display until after the boundary.
A policy table supports more data kinds but expands the required configuration and review result.
open_points.requirement:
The second release
(R0-100) gives it a read-only review page in the owner interface: the
customers whose relationship ended, and the archived projects archived, longer
ago than periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule.

open_points.subject: R0-96 manifest descriptions
open_points.text:
the description of the room name and the alias in Registry's manifest
  record (R0-96).
open_points.question: Which manifest fields carry the writer restriction, and must the room-name and alias descriptions state the complete forbidden-content rule or refer to another governed text?
options: Put the complete rule in each input field's description.
Put one reusable policy reference on both fields.
Describe the rule at operation level for rooms and model level for aliases.
open_points.default_guess: Put the complete writer rule in each affected input field's description.
consequences: Inline descriptions ensure the agent receives the rule wherever it writes the value but duplicate text.
A reference avoids duplication but works only if Kernel reliably supplies the referenced policy to the agent.
Operation- or model-level text may be omitted from a generated binding prompt unless its contract guarantees propagation.
open_points.requirement:
the description of the room name and the alias in Registry's manifest
  record (R0-96).

open_points.subject: R0-92 Registry-to-Kernel trace correlation
open_points.text:
Whether Kernel writes the
key it gives as that request id into its trace record, so that a room or
pointer leads to exactly one node execution, is Kernel's to state in its
case; until it does, the link is one-directional.
open_points.question: Will Kernel persist Registry's request id in each relevant node trace, and if so, what uniqueness guarantee makes the correlation exactly one node execution rather than several retries?
options: Persist it and require one logical node execution per request id, with retries belonging to that execution.
Persist it on every retrying execution, allowing several trace records for one request id.
Do not persist it; retain only the stated one-directional relationship.
open_points.default_guess: Persist it once on the logical node execution and attach retries beneath that execution.
consequences: A unique persisted key permits a Registry room or pointer to resolve to one trace execution.
Recording every retry gives one-to-many correlation instead of the stated desired exact link.
Not recording it leaves Registry records unable to lead back to a trace record.
open_points.requirement:
What Registry keeps is the link from its records to that trace: the request
id a room's create carries (State 1 M03) and the publisher, with its session,
and the request id of a pointer's publish (M05, R0-88).

open_points.subject: R0-98 cleanup ordering
open_points.text:
It holds once the owner's earlier machine no longer gives the agent the
objects folder (the cleanup step of the home server's move).
open_points.question: Must deployment complete and verify that cleanup before production start or import, or is a period in which the earlier machine still exposes the objects folder admissible?
options: Make verified cleanup a precondition of production start and import.
Allow production and import first, but prohibit agent operation until cleanup is verified.
Allow cleanup afterward while agents continue operating.
open_points.default_guess: Make verified cleanup a precondition of agent operation, preferably before production start and import.
consequences: A precondition preserves the stated guarantee that object photos do not reach the agent.
Disabling agents permits migration first but requires a separately enforced deployment gate.
Allowing continued agent operation leaves an admissible interval in which the stated safety claim is false.
open_points.requirement:
Photos of the objects — homes — do not reach the
agent either

open_points.subject: A09 service-rights table
open_points.text:
2. The services and their rights:

   | service | operations | highest class |
   |---|---|---|
   | PresuPro | validate a project reference; read a project context; read a customer's billing data; list artifacts; read the latest artifact of a type | `personal_data` |
   | Client Portal | validate a project reference; read a project context; read a project; list rooms; list artifacts; read the latest artifact of a type | `personal_data` |
   | Cabinet | list projects; read a project context; validate a project reference | `personal_data` |
   | Cabinet Kernel | with agent authority only (A10): register an agent session; end an agent session (A11); read the session's access; request access to a project; validate a project reference; read the agent projection; list rooms; add a room; list artifacts; read the latest artifact of a type; publish and withdraw an artifact pointer (R0-88) | `business_confidential` (R0-74) |
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must name the imported data-provider constant that carries the service-rights policy table, while closed vocabularies must be delivered as model enumerations.

open_points.subject: A01 request-id entropy
open_points.text:
an opaque value the caller
   makes, unique for every create it means as new — printable text of at most
   128 characters, made from at least 16 random bytes, as a random UUID is; a
   blank one is missing (A02). That it is random is the caller's duty;
   Registry checks its form only, so the 16 bytes reach no Registry code.
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must give the 16-byte generation requirement a valid path to the owner-interface code that generates request ids, or state that the owner interface uses a model-defined UUID type whose generation guarantee supplies it.

open_points.subject: A13 session-secret length
open_points.text:
The session's identity, its CSRF value and a confirmation value are each at
   least 32 bytes from the operating system's random source; each is compared
   in constant time and never appears in a URL, a log line, a diagnostic or an
   audit entry (R0-29, R0-37).
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must name an imported data-provider constant for the 32-byte minimum used by generated session-value code.

open_points.subject: A17 secret minimum length
open_points.text:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must name the imported data-provider constant that supplies the 32-byte validation threshold.

open_points.subject: A17 temporary store suffix
open_points.text:
under a
   temporary name — the store's name with a suffix the release declares —
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must name the imported data-provider constant that supplies the declared temporary-name suffix.

open_points.subject: A18 backup schedule values
open_points.text:
Every day at
   03:00 UTC, while Registry runs with its service tokens, it
   makes one backup run; a 03:00 that finds Registry stopped, or in an
   owner-only start (rule 9), makes no run, and none is made later in its
   place. The process looks at the clock at least once a minute;
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must name imported data-provider constants for the 03:00 UTC schedule and the maximum one-minute clock-look interval.
